A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same Hessian-free unlearning work, with matching authors, core methodology, and experiments. The main text, mathematical material, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original unlearning experiments, runtime measurements, and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendices C-D.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional membership-inference, repair, and gradient-clipping results in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces explicitly clipped training updates with ordinary SGD, while Appendix E.4 treats clipping as a stabilization choice and confirms its continued experimental use. The central per-sample recollection vectors, HVP computation, and additive unlearning mechanism remain. The new HVP pseudocode elaborates an existing component.

E1.justification: The MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR-10, LFW, and CelebA coverage and underlying classification tasks remain. Section 6 and Appendix D.4 extend evaluation to training-membership and deletion-membership inference, introducing adversarial scenarios with access to a single model or paired model releases.

E2.justification: FineTune and NegGrad join the large-model application comparison in v4 Table 6, whose counterpart, v3 Table 7, reported only the proposed method. Both baselines already appeared in verification Tables 3-5. The existing NS/IJ comparisons and verification baseline sets are retained.

E3.justification: The reported LR configuration changes from 100 full-batch epochs with L2 coefficient 10^-6 to 15 epochs, batch size 32, and coefficient 0.5. LFW training changes from 49 epochs/batch size 41 to 50/40. Sensitivity sweeps are revised, and adversarial evaluations introduce ROC/AUC and privacy-parameter comparisons. Figure 9's exact settings remain ambiguous because its labels disagree with Appendix E.1.

E4.justification: v4 adds membership-inference robustness analyses across deletion rates and attack features, an empirical test of the existing repair strategy, a learning-accuracy versus unlearning-error analysis, and gradient-clipping sensitivity. It revises the epoch and stepsize studies and removes v3's dataset-size ablation and Tables 10-11.

E5.justification: Both versions report seven random seeds and minimum/maximum error bars for the main verification experiments. v4 additionally reports 95% confidence intervals for membership-inference results in Figures 2 and 5. It does not establish an increase in repeated runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Several MNIST and sensitivity results are replaced. For example, HF's LR accuracy in Table 2 changes from 87.75% to 87.50%, and precomputation time from 19.5 to 220 seconds, alongside changed training settings. v4 adds attack, repair, and clipping findings, including substantial deletion-membership leakage at low deletion rates. Dataset-size results disappear, while verification Tables 3-5 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 introduces an explicit twice-continuously-differentiable setting, replaces the clipping-based gradient bound with a bounded-gradient assumption, and revises Theorem 4 with finite-epoch and q < rho conditions. It adds Corollary 5 and revises the generalization bound. The deletion-capacity result changes from n - 4L^2/(gamma lambda) to a reported O(rho^(-n)/sqrt(d)) expression. Appendix C.1 also supplies a new reweighting and chain-rule derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction foreground online deletion without requiring an empirical-risk minimizer, while removing v3's prominent claims about non-smooth objectives and near-identical retraining. The headline precomputation claim changes from O(nd) to O(n^2 d) in Table 1 and the conclusion. These materially revise the advertised applicability and efficiency contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 newly acknowledges that no popular non-convex problem is known to satisfy all Theorem 4 conditions and that most theoretical guarantees still require convexity. The repair strategy is qualified as heuristic without certified guarantees. Section 6 and Appendix D.4 explain why matching retraining can preserve vulnerability to deletion-membership attacks and discuss the limits of noise-based mitigation.

D1.justification: v4 adds explicit HVP pseudocode, documents storage of intermediate training models, and supplies previously unspecified privacy parameters, clipping threshold 10, and large-model noise standard deviation 0.01. It also updates the anonymous code-access link to a named repository. These expand implementation documentation for the existing pipeline; they do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts toward removing empirical-optimality requirements and supporting online updates. Appendix A adds a substantive comparison with Zhang et al. (2024) on certified deep-model unlearning, replacing the earlier broad first-non-convex framing. The new adversarial discussion incorporates Carlini et al. and Chen et al., substantially expanding the paper's relationship to privacy-auditing research.

P1.justification: v4 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, theoretical narrative, and limitations, and adopts a new title. It separates developer and adversary evaluations, moves discussions ahead of proofs in the appendices, and adds an appendix contents page. These are substantial narrative and organizational revisions beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v4 adds attack, repair, learning/unlearning tradeoff, and clipping figures, and redraws several retained sensitivity plots. Table 1 gains an unlearning-guarantee column; v3 Tables 6-7 become an expanded Table 6 with attack-AUC reporting. Dataset-size tables are removed. The document also adopts the ICLR layout and substantially rearranges figure and table placement.

improvement.justification: The direct privacy audits and more candid applicability limits make v4's forgetting claims easier to assess than v3's reliance on distance, correlation, and accuracy evidence. Corrected headline complexity and added implementation details also help. However, removing the dataset-size study and leaving conflicting Figure 9 settings weaken the revision. The stronger replacement theoretical rates alone do not establish improved rigor, so the net quality gain is limited.
